Rosenthal solution for moving heat source: T(r) = T0 + (P/(2*pi*k*r)) * exp(-v*(r+xi)/(2*alpha)). Predicts melt pool depth/width from laser power, scan speed, material conductivity.
DED volumetric build rate: VBR = bead_width * layer_thickness * travel_speed (typical 50-300 cm3/hr DED, 5-50 cm3/hr SLM).
Powder feed: m_dot = rho_packed * A_nozzle * v_carrier. Bound by carrier gas flow and nozzle geometry.
Layer-induced residual stress: sigma_res ~ E * alpha * delta_T * f(constraint). Drives part distortion + cracking risk.
Cooling rate G*R determines microstructure (columnar vs equiaxed). G = thermal gradient, R = solidification velocity.

Material removal rate per pulse: V = (alpha * I_avg * t_pulse) / (rho * h_v) where alpha = absorption coeff, I_avg = avg intensity, h_v = vaporization enthalpy.
Kerf width = focused beam diameter + (HAZ width). Bottom kerf > top kerf (positive taper) due to beam divergence below focus.
Kerf taper t = (D_top - D_bottom) / 2. Decreases with: lower speed, higher pressure, larger orifice. Active 5-axis comp eliminates taper for perpendicular walls.
Pierce time t_p ~ k * (thickness)^n where n = 1.5-2.0 depending on material brittleness; ductile metals require longer pierce due to rebound.
Arc voltage rises ~6-10 V per mm increase in standoff. THC (Torch Height Control) feeds voltage back to maintain constant cut height.
Pierce delay t_d = a + b*thickness; typical 0.3 + 0.05*t (s). Too short = blow-through molten on lens; too long = consumable wear.
